summary:
Re-validated HEAD 6fb88c8. This is the stale re-check after the uat merge (SL-039) and the O-025 and O-027 layout fixes. I tested a freshly published exe on the real C:\ drive (about 3.58M files, 4.43M entries, 663 unreadable folders) and ran the project's Core directly.

What holds:
- The list is correct on real data. Core's LargestFiles.cs is unchanged since my last pass. Scanner.cs changed only to feed SL-039's scanner-thread tracker, and it still runs on the caller's thread, so O-001 still holds.
- All 100 real rows are files at depths 1 to 14, in the correct order, with 100 distinct paths. Every row exists at its shown path, and every logical size equals FileInfo.Length.
- For the 98 rows that can be opened, on-disk equals the handle's AllocationSize. The other two are pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys: both ProbeFailed, open fails with error 32, and their logical sizes match.
- Ranking took 28.7 to 30.8 ms in the app (30.7 ms in the harness), under O-021's 100 ms threshold.
- Build is clean. xUnit 181/181, Fitness 29/29, rules-parity AGREE, WindowCases 25/25, HookCases 2/2.
- SL-040's window cases were renumbered L-001..L-006 to B-001..B-006 in the merge, because SL-039 took the L names. B-007 was added.

Layout at the default 880x600 on real C:\: every list is in view in every ending I drove.
- Finished, unreadable folders closed: LargestFilesList 46.08 px.
- Finished, opened: LargestFilesList 28.30 px, UnreadableList 29.78 px.
- Stopped, opened: LargestFilesList 47.45 px, UnreadableList 42.55 px.
- TopLevelList was 19.26 to 31.26 px in all of these.
- O-024, O-025 and O-027 hold on real data. But finished-and-opened on a system drive leaves one row per list. That is below B-003's own bar ("each keep room for at least two rows", at least 40 px). B-003 passes only because its planted ending texts are shorter than a real drive's.

What does not hold: at the window's allowed minimum of 560x600, a stopped C:\ scan with the unreadable folders opened puts LargestFilesList at 24 px (its MinHeight) with inView false. The list is not on screen in a state a person reaches by clicking. The cause is measured: the Stopped title (561.7 px at 16 px semibold) and the stopped caption (628.8 px) fit on one line at 880 but wrap at 560 (about 486 px of text width). A finished C:\ scan does not wrap further at 560, so it lays out exactly as at 880.

This is O-024's defect shape at a width the window allows. The builder declared it and code review left it to the window-size question. Grading criterion 11 as met over it would repeat my attempt-2 mistake that reflect named, so criterion 11 is graded no and routed to build-slice. The cheap fix the builder already named is to raise MinWidth (the stopped caption needs roughly 700 px of window width), or to derive the floor from the texts.

Loop note: the outcome layout has now been patched per window size four times (O-024, O-025, O-027, now width). The question underneath, what window size the panel must support, is still unanswered.

I changed nothing in the tree. My throwaway width hook, row harness, runner and logs in %TEMP% are deleted.

criteria.criterion: 1. rank the largest files under the scanned root (top level and six folders down; a folder's total larger than any file)

criteria.criterion: 2. cap the list at count (105 files, count 100, ties at the cut)
criteria.how: KeepsExactlyTheCountLargestWhenSizesTieAtTheCut and B-003 (formerly L-003, 'Top 100 of 105') pass. Real C:\: exactly 100 rows, 100 distinct paths, ordered on-disk desc then size desc. The cut is 811,556,864, the same as at attempt 2.

criteria.criterion: 3. list a tree that has nothing to rank
criteria.how: ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList and B-004 (formerly L-004; LargestFilesPanel 37.92 px with the empty caption) pass at HEAD.

criteria.criterion: 4. list a file that has more than one name
criteria.how: AFileWithTwoNamesIsListedOnce passes. On real C:\ the 100 paths are distinct. The real hardlink completeness walk was not repeated this attempt (attempt 2 found only later hardlink names missing), and LargestFiles.cs is unchanged since.
NoRowComesFromALink passes (real file symlink, folder symlink and junction, never skipped). On real C:\, 20,463 links were not followed, and all 100 rows are Kind File at their own paths.

criteria.criterion: 6. rank by space on disk with both sizes shown
criteria.how: RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes passes. The header 'Largest files, by space on disk' and the On disk / Size columns are unchanged in MainWindow.xaml. Real C:\: for all 98 openable rows, on-disk equals the handle's AllocationSize, and logical equals FileInfo.Length for all 100.

criteria.criterion: 7. show where a file is (>260 chars, trailing dot, trailing space, unpaired surrogate)
criteria.how: EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath passes. B-003 draws the surrogate row 0, closed and opened, and exits 0 (70 would mean a throw). Real C:\: all 100 shown paths open through \\?\. No person looked at the rendering.

criteria.criterion: 8. list from a scan that was stopped
criteria.how: AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead and B-005 pass. Three real C:\ stops: Cancelled, 100 rows from the partial store, caption 'Top 100 of 7,272 files scanned in the part read before the scan stopped. ...'. Scanner still returns only after its run loop ends (O-001).

criteria.criterion: 9. start another scan after a list has been shown
criteria.how: B-006 (formerly L-006) passes in both shapes. At the second scan's start LargestFilesPanel is Collapsed with 0 rows, and at the failure ending the list stays empty.

criteria.criterion: 10. state what the list does not cover
criteria.how: B-002 passes. Real C:\ captions: 'Files in 663 unreadable folders are not included.' (finished) and 'Files in 6 unreadable folders are not included.' (stopped).

criteria.criterion: 11. fit the list into the outcome panel (100 rows, surrogate row, unreadable-folders list also filled)
criteria.how: Met at the default 880x600 on real C:\ in every ending driven: finished closed 46.08 px, finished opened 28.30 px, stopped opened 47.45 px, each in view and virtualized (2-3 of 100 built), with UnreadableList and TopLevelList in view. NOT met at the window's allowed MinWidth: at 560x600, a real stopped C:\ scan with the unreadable folders opened leaves LargestFilesList at 24 px, inView false. The stopped title and caption wrap at 560 and take the lists' room. Also, finished+opened on a system drive gives one row per list (28.3/29.8 px), below B-003's own 'at least two rows' bar of 40 px.

criteria.criterion: 12. report what the window shows after a finished scan of a planted tree
criteria.how: B-001 passes. Every real C:\ report carries largestFilesShown, largestFileOnDisk, largestFilesMs, the LargestFiles*/Unreadable* keys and SL-039's TopLevelPanel/TopLevelList/topLevel, with no names or paths.

criteria.criterion: 13. rank a very large scan (4-5 million entries)
criteria.how: Real C:\ stores of about 4.43M entries: largestFilesMs was 28.72, 28.92, 29.12 and 30.79 ms in four app runs, and Top took 30.73 ms in the Core harness. All are under O-021's 100 ms threshold. LargestFilesScaleTests passes.

criteria.criterion: 14. rank a file whose size the scanner had to probe (open and growing, probe failed, online-only placeholder)
criteria.how: Real C:\ list: 98 SizeProbed rows, whose on-disk equals the independent AllocationSize, and 2 ProbeFailed rows (pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys) with matching logical sizes. Online-only files were not re-censused this attempt; attempt 2 found none of 195,356 listed, as on-disk ranking intends. No open-and-growing file was identified on the list; that shape rests on the spike.

obligations.evidence: Owed back to build-slice. 'Fit the list into the outcome panel ... with the unreadable-folders list also filled' holds at 880x600 but not at 560x600, which the window allows (MinWidth 560, MinHeight 600, MainWindow.xaml:5). Real C:\, published exe at 6fb88c8, stopped mid-scan by the project hook (watch + FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=1), window set to 560x600 by a throwaway Loaded class handler (log 'sizechanged actual=560x600'): LargestFilesList 24 px (its MinHeight), inView false. Same stop at 880x600: 47.45 px, inView true. Cause, measured: the Stopped title (561.7 px, 16 px semibold) and the stopped caption (628.8 px) each wrap to a second line at about 486 px of text width, while the outcome row stays at its fixed 328 px floor. The builder measured the same on a planted tree and declared it uncovered. This is O-024's shape (the opened unreadable list takes the largest files off screen), and code review treated the matching height case (O-027) as a major fix. Options already named by the builder: raise MinWidth to where the stopped texts fit (roughly 700 px or more for the caption at C:\ counts), or derive the outcome floor from the texts' measured height. Also, B-003 asserts 'each keep room for at least two rows' (40 px, WindowCases.ps1:1520-1521), but a real finished C:\ ending opened at 880x600 gives 28.3 and 29.8 px. Either B-003 plants an ending as tall as a system drive's, or its two-row claim is corrected to the one row the XAML comment promises.

Re-read after the SL-039 merge. Scanner.Scan is still 'using var io; using var run; return run.Execute()' (Scanner.cs:35-37) on the caller's thread (:12). TopLevelTracker is 'owned by the scanner's thread' and has no thread, task, timer or lock. Its calls sit inside FolderDone/Finish on the run loop. MainWindow awaits the scan before ShowOutcome → ShowLargestFiles (:228, :429). No writer can run while Top reads.

At the default 880x600 on real C:\ with the unreadable folders opened, the largest-files list is not pushed out of view: finished 28.296 px inView, stopped 47.448 px inView (validate attempt 1 measured 0 px here). The same shape still fails at the allowed MinWidth; see O-013.
Real C:\ at 880x600 and 560x600: TopLevelList is in view after every ending driven (finished closed/opened 31.26/19.26 px, stopped opened/closed 19.26/31.26 px). B-007's eight runs pass.

Every real report carries window.TopLevelPanel{visible,actualHeight} and TopLevelList{actualHeight,inView,realizedRows}, plus topLevel counts (e.g. rows 37, unreadable 3, final true, no names). B-007 asserts them.

MainWindow.xaml:5 MinHeight=600 (was 400), so the window cannot be made shorter than the height B-007 passes at. B-007's MinHeight runs log 'sized height=600 minHeight=600', with every list in view. Heights below 600 are no longer reachable, which replaces my attempt-2 failures at 880x560 and 560x400.
B-006 (formerly L-006) passes both shapes on the merged window. The second scan's start collapses LargestFilesPanel with 0 rows, and at the failure ending it holds no rows.

not_reached: No person looked at the window. Row rendering (wrapped paths, the lone-surrogate name, column alignment) and the one-row-per-list state were judged only from report metrics.

Non-100% DPI, larger text scaling, Windows 10, and displays whose work area is under 600 DIPs (e.g. 768 px tall at 125%). There the window's new MinHeight cannot fit, and text heights, and so the list's room, would differ.
Window sizes other than 880x600 and 560x600, e.g. maximized, or widths between 560 and 880 where the stopped caption starts wrapping.
The on-disk sizes of pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys: opening either fails unelevated with error 32. Only their logical sizes were compared, and no named elevated operation reads a file's allocation.
An independent completeness walk was not repeated at this HEAD. The last one (attempt 2, 658ed6a) skipped cloud-reparse folders, and the guard refused a walk under OneDrive.
An open-and-growing file was not identified as a row on the real list. That shape rests on the spike open-growing-file-stale-directory-size.
The contents of the 663 unreadable folders on C:\, which the list cannot include. read-denied-folders returns counts only.
Drives other than NTFS C:\ (exFAT/FAT removable media, a mapped SMB share) with the list shown. N-001..N-004 were not run.
